description: Retry-After parsing. The server only ever emits delta-seconds with a minimum of 1, on the rate-limited responses of both the ping route and the REST API. The date forms are here because an intermediary may rewrite the header and because the HTTP specification requires a recipient to accept all of them. The parsed value is reported to the caller and never used to schedule an automatic retry: a rate-limited response is not retried. Every case supplies its own clock, so no vector reads a real one.

cases.why: Zero is a valid delta and must not be confused with absent. A parser that returns a falsy value for both makes 'retry now' indistinguishable from 'no guidance'.
Optional whitespace around a header value is stripped by the framing rules, but a client reading a raw header map may still see it.
One over the range. Reporting an absurd value is worse than reporting none: it will be rendered to a user or fed to a sleep.
delta-seconds is a run of digits with no sign, so this is not a delta at all — unlike a past date, which is a valid header that clamps to 0.
A permissive numeric parse accepts this and yields 3.5, which then reaches a caller that expects an integer.

The same ASCII-only digit rule the ping surface uses, applied here for consistency across the fleet. A language whose integer parser or digit predicate is Unicode-aware would otherwise read this as 5.
Header parsing never throws. A malformed header on an error response must not turn into a second, different error.
Clock skew between the server and the client routinely produces this. It clamps to 0, never to a negative number and never to null.
7.6 seconds of real distance rounds down to 7 whole seconds. Rounding up here would be defensible; the contract picks down so both languages agree, and the caller is told this is a floor.

The zone token is mandatory and is always GMT. A lenient date parser will read this as local time and produce an answer that is wrong by the host's UTC offset — silently correct in CI and wrong in production.
The range rule applies to the date branch too, not only to the delta branch.
Obsolete, two-digit year, and still required to be accepted on receipt.
The third required form, with the double space that pads a single-digit day. No zone token appears in it; it is GMT by definition.
